sections.h2: What sets Thomas County apart in southwest Georgia?
sections.html:
Thomas County borders Florida and centers on Thomasville, which is both seat and biggest town. Lawmakers carved it out of Decatur and Irwin counties on December 23, 1825, and the later counties of Colquitt, Brooks and Grady each took a slice of its first boundaries, per Wikipedia.

Of its 552 square miles, only 7.6 are water. Rain in the northwest half runs to the Ochlockonee River, the northeastern edge sends water toward the Suwannee, and the southeast drains to the Aucilla, which begins here. The Red Hills region is centered on the county. Across the line to the south lie Jefferson and Leon counties in Florida, and the Georgia neighbors are Colquitt, Brooks, Grady and Mitchell.

Beyond Thomasville the map holds Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs and Pavo as cities and Ochlocknee as a town. Barwick and Pavo spill over into Brooks County, and Meigs reaches into Mitchell. Public education is split between Thomasville City Schools within the city limits and Thomas County Schools for the rest. A house on one side of that boundary draws a different set of school-minded buyers than one a few blocks over.

sections.h2: How do Thomas County home prices compare with its neighbors?
sections.html:
Homeowners hold a solid majority here, and prices run higher than in the other three counties covered in this set of guides. QuickFacts reports 63.8% owner-occupancy for 2020-2024.

The 2020 count was 45,798 people, and the mid-2025 estimate is 46,368, which is growth of 1.3% on the estimates base. The county has 18,684 households, and 21.0% of residents are past their 65th birthday. Builders pulled just 203 permits in 2025, so an older Thomasville bungalow faces little new-construction competition.

sections.h2: Which offices bill and value property in Thomas County?
sections.html:
The work is split between two offices. The tax commissioner sends bills and takes payment. The board of tax assessors places a value on each parcel and receives exemption applications.

You can reach the county's tax commissioner at 225 N. Broad Street, Thomasville 31792, or by mail at P.O. Box 2175, Thomasville 31799. The number is (229) 225-4136. The counter is staffed on weekdays, opening at 8 in the morning and closing at 5, and a holiday closing list is posted on the site.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, delinquent balances, payoff amounts before a tax sale
  • Tax assessor: values, returns, homestead filings, appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens
  • Seven city tax departments: Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville bill their own residents

The county page explains who sets what. County commissioners pick the county rate, the school board picks the school rate, and the state sets its own by law. Someone living in Thomasville may see a city bill on top of the county one, so ask both offices what is owed.

sections.h2: When is Thomas County property tax due?
sections.html:
Every year the due date is November 15, and the county accepts anything postmarked by then. Per the county's information page, not receiving a bill does not remove the obligation.

Past-due balances are recalculated on the 16th of each month, so a payoff quote expires with the month. Mobile homes pick up penalties each April 2. The county page also states that failing to file a required return costs 10% of the value that went unreported, plus interest.

  • Regular property tax: November 15
  • Mobile home penalties: added April 2
  • Past-due totals: change on the 16th
  • Unfiled return: 10% of unreported value plus interest

The tax commissioner chooses when to hold tax sales, once or twice a year, and the office asks you to phone for the exact amount before a sale. A figure printed on last year's bill will not match.

sections.h2: How does a Thomas County sale handle tax still owed?
sections.html:
Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's bill. The state revenue department says Georgia does not refund tax for part of a year, so a deed signed on January 2 still leaves the full year with the earlier owner.

Most often the closing attorney requests the balance from the tax commissioner and pays it out of the seller's proceeds, or the contract spreads the year across both parties. Request the figure in writing, and ask whether a city bill is also open. Unpaid tax can become a lien filed with the superior court clerk, and a buyer's title company will insist that it be cleared before funds move.

When a house is behind on tax and also needs repairs, an as-is buyer can absorb both and settle the balance at the table. That saves listing prep. It does not erase the debt, because the county is paid either way.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Thomas County value?
sections.html:
Put the challenge in writing to the board of tax assessors. The clock is 45 days, counted from the mailing date on the assessment notice. That deadline comes from the Georgia Department of Revenue, and the county page points to O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 for the right to appeal.

State guidance allows four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. The form must say how you want to proceed, from three choices: an equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. If the assessors and the owner cannot agree, the county page says the appeal moves along to the Board of Equalization on its own. Objections to the tax rate are not part of a value appeal.

  • Deadline: 45 days from the notice mailing
  • Where to file: the assessors' office
  • If unresolved: Board of Equalization, then court

Assessed value is set at 40% of market value, measured on the January 1 valuation date. The county page defines market value broadly enough to include a short sale, bank sale or auction sale, and a distressed sale of your own home can therefore serve as evidence.

sections.h2: Which Thomas County exemption should you confirm before listing?
sections.html:
Homestead is the main one, and the form goes to the tax assessor. The county cutoff is April 1. A filing that arrives later starts with the following year.

Applications may come in at any point during the year, but April 1 is the line for the current bill. The county says it grants local homestead relief that beats the state version, and the assessor can quote today's amounts. Ask for them directly instead of guessing.

Before you list, confirm the exemption sits on the parcel. A lender and a closing attorney will read the bill, and a missing exemption makes the number look larger than it should. The next owner has to apply for themselves, since a sale partway through the year does not carry your filing forward.

faqs.q: Which phone reaches the Thomas County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Dial (229) 225-4136. The office sits at 225 N. Broad Street in Thomasville and takes calls on weekdays between 8 in the morning and 5 in the evening Ask for the assessor's office if your question concerns value or an exemption.

faqs.q: What is the Thomas County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: November 15 each year, with mail postmarked by that day accepted. Overdue amounts change on the 16th of every month, and mobile home penalties begin April 2.

faqs.q: Will selling erase this year's tax in Thomas County?
faqs.a: No. Georgia returns nothing for a partial year, so the January 1 owner carries that bill. At closing the attorney typically settles it out of the seller's proceeds, or the contract shares it.

faqs.q: How many days does an assessment appeal allow in Thomas County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date the notice went out in the mail. Write to the assessors, and mark your preferred hearing path on the state form.

faqs.q: Does Thomasville bill its own tax separately?
faqs.a: Yes. The county tax commissioner's page says Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville each collect their own city taxes. Contact that city's tax department for the city portion.
